messages:
Anna Li: Hey all — ran into a Cloudflare Workers failure when trying our JS SDK sample app. Error is "Buffer is not defined" and later a complaint about `require` being undefined. Anyone seen this?
Mike Roberts: yep, Workers is a strict Web runtime (no Node built-ins, no require). Our SDK still bundles some Node deps.
Timothy Ng: quick repro? is this the sample that uses `node-fetch` + `form-data`? those are common culprits.
Anna Li: sample uses fetch from node-fetch in the helper, and a tiny helper using Buffer.from(base64, 'base64'). It works in Node but fails on deploy. stack: `ReferenceError: Buffer is not defined` then `ReferenceError: require is not defined`
Sophia Chen: for Buffer you can switch to web APIs: `const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(str), c=>c.charCodeAt(0))` or use TextEncoder/TextDecoder depending on direction. For base64 encoding/decoding: `globalThis.atob` / `btoa` (but watch binary).
Mike Roberts: agree. More generally we should ship an ESM edge build that avoids Node-only shims. Wrapping `if (typeof Buffer !== 'undefined')` hacks are brittle tho.
Timothy Ng: also watch usage of `process.env` and `setTimeout` semantics. Workers has a global `setTimeout` but no long-running timers for auth refresh that rely on background timers — they get killed.
Anna Li: good point — our SDK background token refresher does `setInterval` to refresh tokens. That won't work on Workers edge function where invocation short-lived. Any recommended pattern?
Sophia Chen: switch to on-demand refresh: if token expired, call refresh synchronously on request path. Or return 401 to caller and let client retry. For serverless edges, prefer stateless short-lived tokens.
Jake O'Neill: Wranger tip: enable the latest compatibility_date and use the ESM module target. Also avoid `require()` — build with esbuild target=es2020 and externalize node:buffer so you don't accidentally pull polyfills.
Mike Roberts: we should add an SDK shim that detects edge with `typeof globalThis?.WebSocket !== 'undefined' && typeof process === 'undefined'` or maybe check `globalThis.fetch && !globalThis.process`? then provide small implementations for: randomUUID (use crypto.randomUUID or fallback to subtle), base64 helpers, and use fetch directly instead of node-fetch.
Anna Li: can we add that shim without breaking Node consumers? feature-detect at runtime and export both ESM and CJS bundles?
Sophia Chen: yes — simplest is dual outputs: `dist/browser.mjs` (edge-friendly) and `dist/node.cjs`. The package.json `exports` map can point to the right entry for `import` vs `require`. For Workers recommend using the `.mjs` path.
Timothy Ng: typing gotcha: some customers using TS see "DOM" lib missing when targeting node. We should document `tsconfig` for Workers: include "DOM", "ES2021" libs so `fetch`, `Request`, `Response`, `crypto` types exist.
Mike Roberts: note: `crypto.subtle` in Workers is WebCrypto; usage differs from Node's `crypto`. Add helpers and typings to abstract that.
Devex-Bot: Related doc: https://redwood-internal.example.com/devex/edge/sdks#workers-compat — added Jake's wrangler tips and Sophia's dual-build notes. :white_check_mark:
Anna Li: thanks — I'll push a PR to convert the sample to use the edge-mjs entry and remove node-fetch. Will also replace Buffer usage with lightweight base64 helpers shown above.
Jake O'Neill: if you want I can add a small `edge-shim.ts` to our samples repo that exports `encodeBase64`, `decodeBase64`, `randomUUID`, and a `isEdge()` helper. keeps sample tiny.
Anna Li: please do. Also adding a short note in onboarding guide about "Edge runtime differences: no node APIs, prefer edge build" so new users don't trip on this.
Sophia Chen: one more: watch CSR vs SSR bundles. Cloudflare Pages Functions can inject polyfills; Workers should remain tiny. try to avoid pulling `uuid` package unless its ESM-only tiny build.
Timothy Ng: thanks everyone. PR incoming.
Anna Li: updating thread with PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
